glossary.Cranial vault: The bony box of the skull that holds the brain.
glossary.Cerebral perfusion: Blood flow delivering oxygen and nutrients to the brain.
glossary.Intracranial haemorrhage: Bleeding inside the skull, for example subarachnoid, subdural or intracerebral bleeds.
glossary.CNS: Central nervous system: the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.Idiopathic intracranial hypertension: Raised ICP with no lesion or obvious cause, typically in young women with obesity.
glossary.BMI: Body mass index: weight in kg divided by height in metres squared; above 30 is obese.
glossary.Nerve palsy: Weakness or paralysis of the muscles supplied by a nerve.
glossary.Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing heard in the ears without an outside sound.
glossary.Seizures: Episodes of abnormal, excessive brain electrical activity causing fits or altered awareness.
glossary.Posturing: Abnormal rigid limb positions (flexion or extension) in severe brain injury, a sign of deep coma.
glossary.Bradycardia: Heart rate below 60 beats per minute.
glossary.Contraindicated: Should not be done because the harm is likely to outweigh the benefit.
glossary.Brainstem: The base of the brain linking to the spinal cord; controls breathing, heart rate and consciousness.
glossary.Brainstem herniation: The brainstem being forced downward through the foramen magnum by pressure from above.
glossary.Venous outflow obstruction: A blockage to blood draining out of the brain, raising pressure inside the skull.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging; a detailed scan using magnets, better than CT for soft tissue.
glossary.Theatre: The operating theatre, where surgery is done.
glossary.Vasoconstriction: Narrowing of blood vessels, reducing the blood volume they hold.
glossary.Osmotherapy: Giving concentrated solutions such as mannitol or hypertonic saline to pull water out of the brain.
glossary.Neurosurgical: To do with brain and spine surgery.
glossary.ABCDE: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure: the structured emergency assessment.
glossary.Escalation: Calling for more senior help or a higher level of care.
glossary.CSF diversion: Draining CSF away, for example with an external drain or shunt, to relieve hydrocephalus.
glossary.Stroke pathway: The fast-track hospital route for assessing and treating stroke.
glossary.Compensation: The body adjusting one thing (here, pushing out CSF and venous blood) to offset another.
glossary.Sympathetic: The fight-or-flight nervous system that raises heart rate and blood pressure.
glossary.Osmotic gradient: A difference in solute concentration that draws water towards the more concentrated side.
glossary.Vascular compartment: The space inside the blood vessels.
glossary.Ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue, starving it of oxygen.
glossary.Arterial CO2: The level of carbon dioxide in arterial blood; high levels dilate brain vessels.
glossary.Cerebral blood volume: The amount of blood held in the brain's vessels at any time.
glossary.Pressure gradient: A difference in pressure between two spaces that pushes contents from high to low.
